title: FeverON - Registry for pediatric oncology patients with non-neutropenic fever
summary:
Fever is a common occurrence in the treatment of children, adolescents and young adults with cancer. When neutrophils are low, patients have a high risk for a complicated course of fever in the event of an infection. Therefore, all of these patients are promptly admitted to the hospital and treated with antibiotics. National and international guidelines and treatment recommendations are readily available for the treatment of neutropenic fever.

Less is known about the course of patients undergoing chemotherapy with non-neutropenic fever. In this group, only a small portion of patients become severely ill and need temporary treatment in the intensive care unit. The exact percentage of patients with non-neutropenic fever who need to be hospitalized and/or treated with antibiotics is not yet precisely known. For some of these patients, outpatient antibiotic therapy might be an option, or it might even be possible to forgo antibiotic therapy altogether. 

Non-neutropenic fever is common. About half of all fever episodes in patients undergoing chemotherapy occur during phases without neutropenia. However, there is a lack of robust data to create guidelines and treatment recommendations for non-neutropenic fever. 

This registry is intended to collect pseudonymized data that will help us analyze risk factors for severe courses of such non-neutropenic fever episodes. Data collection includes results of pathogen diagnostics, the course of the fever episode, severe courses (e.g. treatment in an intensive care unit), and details of the management of each fever episode (inpatient or outpatient, with or without antibiotics). Only data from routine clinical activities will be collected. 

The aim of the registry is to collect reliable data that can aid in improving treatment for this cohort of patients. This could result in a more selective and restrictive use of antibiotics in patients who truly need antibiotic therapy. The pseudonymized data collected in this registry will serve as a historical comparison group in later intervention studies.

interventions.name:
Observation group: 
Prospective data analysis of all pediatric oncology patients with non-neutropenic fever (temperature ≥ 38.5°C oder persistent temperature ≥ 38°C) with non-neutropenia (ANC ≥0.5 x 109/L) (NNF), age 0 - 18 years old during or not longer than six weeks post oncologic therapy

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Cancer diagnosis, oncologic treatment or at most six weeks post oncologic treatment, non-neutropenic fever (temperature of once 38.5°C or more or persistent temperature of at least 38°C and at least 500/µl neutrophils and no decrease in neutrophils <500/µl within the following 72 hours).
Exclusion criteria:
Previous allogenic hematopoetic stem cell transplant or CART cell therapy
